subject: Capacity & SDK discovery — capacity numbers and technical deep-dive
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Zoe Patterson <zoe@finovate-payments.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: capacity & SDK plan + next steps

Thanks again for a productive call today — really appreciate Zoe and Alan walking us through the payment flows and peak-hour behavior. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on a technical deep-dive next week.

High-level notes from the call:
- Primary workload: authorization + fraud-score enrichment + receipts generation. Expected peak: ~420 reqs/sec for the auth path, average payload ~2.2k tokens.
- Embeddings/reranker: customer search + post-auth FAQ resolution, ~120qps for embeddings lookup, re-ranker called per top-N candidate (N=6).
- SLA target: P95 < 220ms for auth path; best-effort for reranker (P95 < 400ms).

Technical asks / follow-ups (we'll treat these as action items):
1) SDK bootstrap & auth: you noted API-key-based service tokens today; please confirm if you'd prefer short-lived per-route tokens or a service account with scoped API key for the dedicated cluster. We can support both; per-route tokens give better audit granularity.
2) Routing & variants: confirm whether you want latency-first routing (for live auth) and cost-fallback routing to a smaller-quantized model for non-critical paths (receipts).
3) Structured output / tool-calling: receipts generation will use Redwood function-calling style. We need example schema for the invoice/receipt format and a sample of third-party tool endpoints (if applicable).
4) Embeddings + reranker architecture: we propose an ANN index + a lightweight reranker hosted on the same dedicated pool to avoid cross-network hops. Need your expected vector dims and whether you will host vector DB (we support bringing-your-own or provide managed).
5) Dedicated capacity sizing: please confirm sustained QPS, expected burst factor, and concurrency per request type. We drafted a starter throughput workbook — attached.

Attachments I pushed after the call: rdw_mvp_throughput_estimate_v2.xlsx (workbook with initial sizing), redwood-sku-matrix.csv (SKU/instance guidance).

Proposed next steps:
- You share exact qps/concurrency numbers and security contact for SOC2/compliance questions by Tue EOD.
- Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with your infra + security team (suggest Wed or Thu next week). Calendly link below.
- We (Marcus + Dev) will prepare a short ops runbook with pre-warm steps and autoscale threshold proposals for the dedicated pool.

Thanks — I can send a mutual action plan PDF and calendar invite once we lock times.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks Kimberly — great write-up. A few clarifications from our side:
- Capacity: the 420 reqs/sec is peak sustained for the auth microservice during US business hours (we handle global routing but this is the US card flow). We have an additional ~60qps steady-state for search/rerank.
- Burst: up to 2x sustained for marketing spikes (~10 minutes).
- Concurrency: our callers open ~6 concurrent streams per logical session for multi-step auth flows.

Two specific items for the deep-dive: pre-warm strategy (how quickly can a dedicated pool ramp?) and cold-start behavior for the embedded reranker. Also, we use short-lived JWTs internally — is there a recommended mapping to Redwood's token model?

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Zoe Patterson <zoe@finovate-payments.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Recap: capacity & SDK plan + next steps

Thanks Zoe — quick technical clarifications from the infra side. High-level recommendations to map your numbers to dedicated capacity: 

1) Concurrency & per-GPU guidance:
- For auth (short responses, <500 tokens), we recommend targeting 10-16 concurrent requests per GPU for an int8-quantized variant; that maps to ~100-160 qps per A100-class GPU depending on observed token latency.
- For reranker (larger compute per call because of cross-encoder), isolate reranker on separate nodes with 4-6 concurrency per GPU or run as small batch microservice with batch-size 8. Co-locating on same VPC with routing rules is fine.

2) Queues & batching:
- Use a front-door request queue with two priority lanes: auth (low-latency, priority=high) and background (rerank/indexing). Configure queue depth at 3x expected concurrency to absorb jitter.

3) Autoscale policy (starter template):
- Scale-up trigger: sustained GPU util > 75% for 60s or queued requests > 60 for 30s.
- Scale-down: util < 30% for 5m with staggered cool-down (min up-time 10m).
- Pre-warm: warm standby nodes provisioned in <90s if pre-warm pool set to 10% of baseline; full scale to target in ~3-5 minutes depending on cloud provisioning.

4) Auth model mapping:
- Short-lived JWTs: map these to short-lived Redwood scoped tokens via our token-exchange endpoint (we can issue per-route tokens that inherit JWT claims). This gives audit-friendly logs and per-route quotas.

5) Embeddings & reranker integration:
- If you manage the vector DB, we recommend approximate nearest neighbor (HNSW) with an external index in your VPC and a fast gRPC bridge to Redwood; reranker stays in the dedicated pool and reads top-K candidates.
- If you prefer managed vector DB, we can host an index and replicate embeddings for read locality.

I've also attached a quick throughput worksheet (small edits to the workbook you sent) and a starter autoscale JSON we use for Dedicated templates. Happy to walk through these in the deep-dive.

—Marcus
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
